title: Premium Accounting Standard: Ten-Pay Billing, Grace Period and Lapse of Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance
content:
# Ten-pay premiums on Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance

## Clauses

**1. Billing.** Ten-pay premiums on an Ashgrove CareAssure policy are billed for the tier's number of ten-pay policy years, in annual mode at the annual-mode multiplier or by monthly EFT at the monthly EFT multiplier, on a draft day from the 1st to the tier's latest EFT draft day.

**2. Status in which money is applied.** A remittance is applied as premium only while the policy status is Applied, In Force or Grace Period. This is judged from the policy's status on the company's record.

**3. Small shortfalls and overpayments.** A remittance short by up to the tier's shortfall tolerance is applied as full payment, and unapplied money above the tier's overpayment refund threshold is refunded.

**4. Grace period.** When an installment is unpaid on its due date the policy enters a grace period of the tier's grace period length, counted in calendar days.

**5. Cure within grace.** The overdue premium must be received no later than the last day of grace, which is the unpaid installment's due date plus the grace period length. The last day of grace is found by adding the grace period length in calendar days to the due date; a remittance received on that day is in time. The due date is the unpaid installment's due date as the policy record shows it in the paid-to date. A remittance received in time returns the policy from Grace Period to In Force.

**6. Lapse notice.** The policy cannot lapse until the third-party notice period has run after a lapse notice has been mailed to the owner and to the designated third party. The lapse date is the day after the later of the last day of grace and the end of that notice period.

**7. Effect of lapse.** On lapse, a policy whose premiums were paid for at least the tier's shortened benefit minimum of policy years continues under the shortened benefit period — long-term care benefits limited to total premiums paid less benefits already paid, with no death benefit beyond the residual death benefit — and otherwise lapses without value.

**8. Completion.** When the last ten-pay installment is paid the policy becomes Paid Up.

**9. Designee changes.** The owner may change the third-party designee at any time.

**Premiums paid** means, for any date, the total of the remittances applied as premium on the policy from the issue date to that date, less any premium refunded as overpayment.

## The grace and notice clock — worked dates (hypothetical; CareAssure tiers carry a 61-day grace period and a 30-day notice period)

| Unpaid installment due | Last day of grace | Lapse notice mailed | End of notice period | Later of the two | Lapse date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March 2026 | 10 May 2026 | 1 May 2026 | 31 May 2026 | 31 May 2026 | 1 June 2026 |
| 10 March 2026 | 10 May 2026 | 5 April 2026 | 5 May 2026 | 10 May 2026 | 11 May 2026 |

Boundary of clause 5 on the first row: a remittance received on 10 May 2026 is in time and cures the grace period; a remittance received on 11 May 2026 is not in time.

## Clause 7 — positive and negative cases (hypothetical policies)

| Policy years for which premiums were paid | Premiums paid | Benefits already paid | Position on lapse |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | $24000.00 | $0.00 | Shortened benefit period; long-term care benefits limited to $24000.00 |
| 3 | $18000.00 | $5000.00 | Shortened benefit period; long-term care benefits limited to $13000.00 |
| 2 | $12000.00 | $0.00 | Lapses without value |

## Clauses 2 and 3 — points of judgement

- A remittance received on a policy that is Paid Up, Lapsed, Surrendered or in any status other than Applied, In Force or Grace Period is not applied as premium.
- With a $2.00 tolerance, a remittance $1.75 short is applied as full payment; one $2.25 short is not.
- With a $25.00 threshold, $40.00 of unapplied money is refunded; $25.00 is not above the threshold.
